videos.title: US Midterms Test Trumpism as One Nation Surges in Australia
videos.description:
The US midterms will test President Trump's political power at home and offer clues about the staying power of Trump-style politics globally. In Australia, the far-right One Nation party is surging in popularity with policies that echo Trump's agenda, including opposition to immigration and climate-change skepticism. United States Studies Centre Economic Security Director Hayley Channer joins "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" to discuss what the US vote could mean for Trumpism abroad and the outlook for US-Australia relations.

videos.title: Kumar: Costs, ICE Are Pushing Latinos Toward Democrats
videos.description:
Maria Teresa Kumar, President and CEO of Voto Latino, says Latino voters in Texas’ Rio Grande Valley who moved toward President Trump over the economy and border security are now being pushed back toward Democrats by high costs, tariffs and immigration enforcement. Kumar says businesses in the region are being hurt by workers being picked up by Border Patrol and ICE and by uncertainty over tariff costs. Kumar says Latino voters in Florida are also rethinking their support after the administration rescinded protections for people with Temporary Protected Status. Kumar says Democrats cannot take Latino turnout for granted and need an affordability agenda as well as accountability over ICE detention and enforcement. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power."
--------

videos.title: Robinhood CFO on Retail IPO Demand, Agentic Trading
videos.description:
Robinhood is competing with other retail brokerages over access to Anthropic's mega-IPO and others as they come to market. CFO Shiv Verma says the company continues to see demand for IPO access, adding, "We're making sure the companies know retail is here." He also discusses the use of AI agents in trading accounts, saying customers continue asking for more agentic tools. Verma also says Robinhood is seeing an increase in non-sports related trades on its prediction market platform. Plus, Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Kate Sullivan joins to discuss President Trump's remarks from the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool just one day before midterm elections. Then, Satya Thallam, Former Senior Counselor in the Trump White House joins to discuss data center opposition as a major issue in the election. Finally, Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY) joins to discuss his campaign strategy as New Yorkers head to the polls Tuesday.

videos.title: Apple Sales Meet Estimates, China Is a Weak Spot
videos.description:
Apple posted September quarter revenue that narrowly topped analysts’ estimates, even as sales in the key Chinese market fell short of projections. Revenue rose 12% to $114.5 billion during the fiscal fourth quarter, which ended Sept. 26, the company said in a statement. Analysts had estimated $113.5 billion on average, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The quarterly report — the first under new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus — offered a mixed picture to investors. Sales growth decelerated from a 16% clip in the June quarter, and results from Apple’s iPad and wearables businesses were particularly weak. But the iPhone, the company’s biggest moneymaker, remained strong. Mark Gurman, Bloomberg News Managing Editor for Global Consumer Tech, joins to discuss the results. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec.

He discusses the importance of getting the fundamentals of digital development right, including electricity, connectivity, affordability and digital public infrastructure, and shares examples of how locally relevant AI tools are being used in agriculture, health and education.

videos.title: The Race To Power AI Is Reshaping America's Electric Grid
videos.description:
AI data centers are driving unprecedented demand for electricity and putting renewed pressure on America’s power grid to modernize its equipment and develop greener, more efficient sources of power. Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon are all spending millions of dollars on local infrastructure upgrades and companies like SpaceXAI are even building off-grid power plants to power their data centers.

Google says its planned 780-megawatt data center in Pine Island, Minnesota, could offer a model for powering the AI boom. In a proposed agreement with Xcel Energy, Google says it will support 1,900 megawatts of new wind, solar and battery capacity, while minimum payments and exit fees are intended to protect local ratepayers if demand falls short.

CNBC examines whether projects like Pine Island can make the grid cleaner without shifting costs to existing customers, why some energy experts argue that smaller data centers could make better use of infrastructure already in place, and how utilities’ financial incentives can complicate efforts to build less.

videos.title: Why Fuel Economy Rollbacks Will Spur More Trucks, More V-8 Engines
videos.description:
Lowered compliance costs, greater control over products, more big engines, more pickup trucks. These are just some of the changes investors expect from the rollback of fuel economy rules and the elimination of fines. Data indicate pent up demand for pickup trucks, and many automakers are bringing back V-8 engines. At the same time, hybrid vehicles are surging, and electric vehicles have longer term structural demand in their favor.
